title: Selector Stressbench: synthetic regression pipeline for function routing and argument integrity
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem statement: configuration flips (quantization, routing policies, kernel selection) and model upgrades cause subtle regressions in which function/tool a model chooses and in the correctness of the arguments it emits. These regressions can be high-cost in production (incorrect API calls, downstream failures). Goal: build a synthetic, repeatable regression pipeline (Selector Stressbench) that injects realistic config/model deltas, exercises function-selection policies, and validates both selection accuracy and argument integrity with deterministic checks and fuzzy scoring.

Scope: daily automated runs across staged model variants (hosted, dedicated-compatible, and quantized variants) and across a matrix of config changes (batching limits, fallback policy, routing heuristic weights). The pipeline will produce per-change deltas for: selection-precision/recall, argument-schema pass-rate, argument-value plausibility (light-weight heuristics), and a small set of human-review candidates when the regression signal is marginal.

Approach:
- Synthetic workload generation: create ~20k intent-to-tool mappings derived from production call traces (sanitized) + fuzzed paraphrases and adversarial templates.
- Config delta injection: automatically mutate routing weights, enable/disable cache, toggle quantization profiles, and swap model variants in the test harness.
- Orchestration: use the existing eval runner (extend runner to support function-metadata and arg-schema checks) and run in parallel across model variants.
- Checks: deterministic match for expected tool selection where ground truth exists; fuzzy scorer for ambiguous prompts; JSON schema validation for arguments; simple value sanity checks for high-risk fields (URLs, UUIDs, numeric ranges).
- Thresholds & alerting: baseline selection accuracy and arg-pass-rate computed per-route; alert when absolute drop > 2 percentage points and relative drop > 5% over baseline in daily run.
- Outputs: regression report artifact (CSV + JSON summary), Grafana time-series of metrics, an auto-filed PR template with failing examples, and a prioritized human review queue for borderline cases.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline runs on schedule in CI/CD and daily on prod-evals cluster
Synthetic corpus of >=20k sanitized test cases with intent->expected-tool metadata
Detects seeded regressions (we inject controlled changes) with >95% sensitivity for selection faults >3% magnitude
Argument schema validator catches malformed payloads with <1% false positive rate on historical logs
Regression dashboard + alerting rule in Grafana + auto-PR template created on regression detection
Documentation (Confluence) and runbook for triage and rollback created and linked in the pipeline output
notes: 2025-10-29: Kickoff — sketched synthetic generation approach; decided to prioritize high-frequency routes for first phase.
2025-10-31: Design review — PM asked to include human-review sampling for marginal deltas; accepted. (See design doc)
2025-11-02: Implementation note — extended eval-runner to accept function-metadata (schema + canonical examples). PR in progress.
2025-11-04: Security review triage — argument-value heuristics flagged for PII checks; we will run sanitized traces and add masking step. Security review: low risk; documented.
2025-11-05: Integration test — ran against two model variants (rtx-large-v1 and quantized-lite-v1); detected synthetic seed regression as expected (selection accuracy drop from 0.917 to 0.876).
Follow-ups: add per-customer impact weighting to prioritization; evaluate integrating with alert engine to create incidents in the future.
